qaFlags.question: A farmer notices that the underground part of his potato plant swells to store food, while the green part above ground carries water upward and holds the leaves up to the light. Which two parts are being described?
qaFlags.qa_issue: Factually inaccurate: a potato tuber is a modified underground stem, not a root, so labeling the swelling storage part as 'root' is botanically incorrect and could mislead pupils.

lesson.title: Parts of a Plant and Their Jobs
lesson.description: Learners explore the main parts of a flowering plant and what each part does to help it survive.
learningObjectives: Explain the function of roots, stem, leaves and flowers
lesson.content:
Look at a bean plant growing in the school garden. It has roots, a stem, leaves and flowers, and each part has its own special job that helps the plant survive.

Roots grow down into the soil, holding the plant firmly and soaking up water and minerals like a straw. The stem carries this water up to the leaves and flowers, leaves use sunlight to make food, and flowers make seeds for new plants.

Try this: place a celery stalk in a cup of water mixed with food colouring. After a day, cut the stalk and see coloured lines, showing how the stem carries water upward to the leaves.
